## Shared scenes

> The Ashdown children sit in the old [Methodist](../codex/factions.md#methodist) cemetery talking about gravestones, ghosts, and the [Carrow](../character/carrow.md) family. Drawn by the smell of cooked trout, they run down to [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) and join the [Carrow](../character/carrow.md) children for supper, quickly becoming fast friends.
>

> The Ashdown children find a runaway girl named [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) hiding in an old barn near their home. They feed her and listen as she shares her tragic past, her escape from her abusive guardian, and her unique perspectives on life and religion.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P4](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER V. > [Mary Stubbs](../character/mary-stubbs.md) attends church with the manse children using borrowed clothes, making a scene by sticking her tongue out at a parishioner. Refusing to attend school, she cleans the manse, spars with [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) over food, and spends time with the local children at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow). Despite occasional arguments, Mary captivates the children with her stories, ghost tales, and unique tricks.
>

> While their father is away and [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) is bedridden, [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) attempt to clean the house, but accidentally spark a village scandal when they beat carpets in the cemetery, believing it is Monday rather than Sunday.
>

> [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) becomes engrossed in [German](../codex/factions.md#german) theology, neglecting his duties and family. Mrs. Hector Twiss visits the manse and proposes adopting [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md), but Ashdown firmly rejects her offer. Outraged, Mrs. [Twiss](../character/twiss.md) criticizes his parenting before departing, leaving Ashdown deeply shaken and introspective.
>

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. HECTOR TWISS MAKES A CALL P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. > [Grace](../character/grace.md) is furious and heartbroken after [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) slaughters her pet rooster, [Adam](../character/adam.md), to serve to the visiting minister, Mr. Perry. During dinner, [Grace](../character/grace.md) openly dislikes Mr. Perry, who eats [Adam](../character/adam.md) and preaches at her. Later in the study, [Grace](../character/grace.md) secretly watches Mr. Perry's coat-tails catch fire from the hearth, getting revenge on him when he scorches his new coat.
>

> [Grace](../character/grace.md) scandalizes the congregation by wearing boots without stockings to church, drawing sharp criticism from local gossips while [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) and the Carrow girls rush to her defense. To protect her father's reputation and fulfill a punishment imposed by Tobias, [Grace](../character/grace.md) publishes an explanatory letter in the local newspaper detailing why she gave away her last good stockings.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”

> [Grace](../character/grace.md) concludes her letter to the Journal, accepting sole responsibility for attending church without stockings and taking the blame alongside Tobias and [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) for harvesting potatoes from Evan Garrick's field, while clearing the Lew Baxters and the [Carrows](../codex/factions.md#carrows) of any wrongdoing.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”

> The [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club) decides to fast on Sunday as punishment for their graveyard song, which causes [Ida Ashdown](../character/ida-ashdown.md) to faint during the church service. Doctor [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md) and Mrs. Elder Clow help revive her, leading [Grace](../character/grace.md) to explain their self-punishment rule to their distraught father. Realizing how neglected his children are, [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) reflects mournfully on his duties as a father and his unresolved love for [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) before returning to his theological studies.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P0](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P11](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0011), [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P16](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0016), [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P21](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0021)_

> Tobias punishes [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) for running away from a ghost by forcing him to sit on a graveyard tombstone until midnight. [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) endures the chilly rain during his midnight vigil and subsequently falls gravely ill with double pneumonia. After a tense battle for his life, [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) recovers with the support of the community and returns to [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow).
>
